intro: This is a guided inner inquiry — not a test, not a clinical assessment. Each of the ten Sefirot of the Tree of Life corresponds to a quality of soul. Sit with each question. Answer in your own words, as honestly as you can. The AI will then weave your responses into a personal Tree map showing which currents in you are flowing freely, which are developing, and which are blocked — and which single Sefirah is most worth your attention now.
outro: Submit when you have answered every question. You can save partial answers and return; the assessment only completes when all questions have at least a sentence in response.

sefirot.name: Keter
sefirot.title: Crown
sefirot.essence: The apex. Pure being before any attribute. The breath above thought.
questions: Describe a moment when you felt completely beyond thought, identity, and effort — simply existing. How accessible is that state to you?
When you sit in silence with no goal and no task, what arises? Are you comfortable there, or does the mind quickly fill the space?
Have you experienced something you would call 'pure being' — awareness without object? If so, how do you find your way back?

sefirot.name: Chokmah
sefirot.title: Wisdom
sefirot.essence: The first flash. The seed-point of insight before words.
questions: Describe a moment when you knew something was true before you could explain why. How often do you trust that knowing and act on it?
When inspiration strikes, do you welcome it or do you wait for it to be justified first?
Where in your life do you initiate — start things, throw the first spark — versus respond to what others have started?

sefirot.name: Binah
sefirot.title: Understanding
sefirot.essence: The receptive deep. The womb that gives form to wisdom.
questions: When you receive a new insight or idea, how deeply do you develop it before moving on? Do you tend to collect flashes of understanding without fully building them out?
How comfortable are you with sustained, structured contemplation — sitting with one question for hours, days, weeks?
Where in your life do you provide the form, the boundaries, the shape that lets others' ideas become real?

sefirot.name: Chesed
sefirot.title: Loving-kindness
sefirot.essence: Overflowing benevolence. The open hand. Unconditional giving.
questions: How naturally do you extend grace, generosity, and unconditional acceptance to others — including those whose views you find wrong or harmful? Where does that generosity have limits?
When have you given without expecting return — not as performance but because it overflowed naturally? How often does that happen?
Where in your life is your kindness unbounded, and where is it conditional? What guards the boundary?

sefirot.name: Geburah
sefirot.title: Severity
sefirot.essence: The holy 'no.' The cutting away. The limit that preserves.
questions: Where in your life do you struggle to set boundaries or cut away what no longer serves? Where do you give more than is healthy because you cannot say no?
Can you discipline yourself without becoming harsh? Where does your structure tip into rigidity?
When have you said the difficult 'no' that another person needed to hear? How did you find the courage?

sefirot.name: Tiferet
sefirot.title: Beauty
sefirot.essence: The heart. The reconciling sun. Where opposites meet without losing themselves.
questions: When do you feel most authentically yourself — not performing, not achieving, simply present and whole? How often does that quality govern your daily life rather than appearing only in rare moments?
How well do you hold opposites in tension without collapsing one into the other — kindness and firmness, joy and grief, doing and being?
Where in your life does the heart's natural compass guide you, and where does it seem distant or unreliable?

sefirot.name: Netzach
sefirot.title: Eternity / Victory
sefirot.essence: The artist's flame. Endurance. Beauty, passion, the natural world.
questions: How connected are you to beauty, passion, and the natural world? Do your emotions flow freely or do you tend to intellectualize your feelings before allowing yourself to experience them?
Where in your life do you persist — keep making, keep loving, keep showing up — without needing external validation to continue?
When you experience awe — a sunset, a piece of music, an act of love — how long does it stay with you?

sefirot.name: Hod
sefirot.title: Splendor
sefirot.essence: The architect. Precision. The right word, the clean structure, Hermes' mind.
questions: How naturally do you organize complex ideas into clear communicable form? Where does your communication sometimes over-explain, under-explain, or miss the mark?
When you analyze a situation, do you stay grounded in what is actually so, or do you spin into abstraction that loses contact with reality?
Where in your life does precision serve you, and where has it become hairsplitting that misses the larger truth?

sefirot.name: Yesod
sefirot.title: Foundation
sefirot.essence: The storehouse. Dreams. The unconscious. What gathers before it descends into the visible.
questions: How much of your inner life — your real beliefs, your genuine spiritual development, your authentic self — is visible in your outer relationships and daily choices? Where is the gap between who you are within and how you appear without?
How attentive are you to your dreams, intuitions, and quieter inner currents? Do you record them, listen to them, take them as guidance?
Where in your life are you living from images and patterns inherited from elsewhere rather than from your own deep ground?

sefirot.name: Malkuth
sefirot.title: Kingdom
sefirot.essence: The world made manifest. The body. The earth. The Shekhinah in her exile and her return.
questions: How well does your outer daily life — your habits, your body, your physical environment, your material circumstances — reflect your inner spiritual development? Where is the gap largest between who you are becoming and how you are living?
Do you bless the ordinary, or do you treat the spiritual as something separate from cooking, cleaning, working, sleeping?
How present are you in your body? When you walk, eat, breathe — are you here, or somewhere else?
